entries.test: Musk's public self-driving predictions from 2015 through May 2022 and documented autonomous-driving capabilities available by May 31, 2022 would test this claim.
entries.note: The statement that the prediction remained unfulfilled is Marcus's own assertion, although it describes Musk's predictions.

entries.test: Published evaluations of contemporary data-driven AI on common versus rare situations would show whether rare events caused substantial reliability problems.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph gives 'serious issue' a concrete meaning: difficulty handling rare events with little training data.

entries.test: Public technical descriptions, driving evaluations, and failure analyses of Tesla's systems as of May 2022 would test whether reliance on learned pattern matching caused substantial difficulty with unexpected situations.
entries.note: The hash-table comparison is figurative, but the underlying architectural and causal assertions are testable. The knowledge qualification is preserved.
The continuation forecast explicitly says 'probably.' Its historical component could be checked separately.
This expresses a judgment about the research direction the field needs to take.
The central commitment is his assessment that reliance on deep learning is unrealistic and more techniques are needed.
'Might well not' expresses a possibility rather than a firm prediction.

entries.test: Public task requirements and capability evaluations for general-purpose domestic robots and autonomous road vehicles would test whether domestic operation requires substantially broader cognitive capabilities.
entries.note: The plain comparison concerns breadth of required capabilities across varied homes and tasks. It does not assert anything specific about Optimus's implementation.

entries.test: A publicly demonstrated AGI achieved without resolving the described integration and patch-induced regression problems would refute the necessity claim, while proposals available in May 2022 would test the accompanying observation.
entries.note: This combines a necessary-condition forecast with a present-tense assessment of proposals. 'I don't think' here introduces an asserted position rather than an explicit probability.

entries.test: Public research and engineering case studies available by May 2022 would test whether deep-learning debugging difficulties stemmed from limited understanding and whether effective fixes existed beyond data collection, added layers, and similar retraining approaches.
entries.note: The sweeping 'nobody' assertion remains factual and can be challenged by documented counterexamples.

entries.test: Public evaluations in 2029 would establish whether AI can reliably answer questions about novels' plots, characters, conflicts, and motivations that require understanding beyond the literal text.
entries.note: The beyond-literal-text qualification comes from the immediately following sentence and is faithfully included.

entries.test: Public evaluations in 2029 using diverse, unselected proofs from mathematical literature would test whether AI can faithfully translate their natural-language arguments into symbolic representations suitable for verification.
entries.note: Success on a few selected proofs would not establish the claimed general capability.
